Standing problem: how healthy is repeat purchasing? Report one metric per row: (1) the share of people (customer_unique_id) with more than one order, across all orders regardless of status; (2) the average number of orders among those repeat customers; (3) the share of item revenue (sum of item price over orders with status 'delivered') that came from repeat customers' orders; (4) the calendar month (YYYY-MM) in which the most people placed their first order. Then say what the numbers mean together. Use these metric identifiers in rows: repeat_customer_share, avg_orders_per_repeat_customer, repeat_revenue_share, month_most_first_orders.

Standing problem: how do delivery performance and customer satisfaction relate? Over orders with status 'delivered' that have a customer delivery date, report one metric per row: (1) the average delivery time in fractional days from purchase to customer delivery; (2) the share of those orders delivered after the estimated delivery date; (3) the average review score of late orders and (4) of on-time orders, averaging over review rows; (5) the customer state (two-letter code) with the longest average delivery time among states with at least 500 such orders. Then say what the numbers mean together, without claiming causes the data cannot show. Use these metric identifiers in rows: avg_delivery_days, late_share, avg_review_score_late, avg_review_score_on_time, slowest_state_500_plus.

Standing problem: which categories and sellers drive performance? Over orders with status 'delivered', report one metric per row: (1) the product category (English name) with the highest item revenue (sum of item price) and (2) that revenue in BRL; (3) the share of item revenue earned by the top 10 sellers; (4) the number of sellers with at least 100 delivered items; (5) the category (English name) with the lowest average review score among categories with at least 500 reviewed delivered orders, counting each order once per category. Then say what the numbers mean together. Use these metric identifiers in rows: top_category_english, top_category_revenue, top10_seller_revenue_share, sellers_with_100_plus_delivered_items, lowest_score_category_500_plus.

Standing question for the 2018-01 run: did delivery performance change materially by customer state? Compare orders purchased in 2018-01 with orders purchased in 2017-12, using orders with status 'delivered' that have a customer delivery date, and the average delivery time in fractional days from purchase to customer delivery. Consider only states (two-letter codes) with at least 200 such orders in both months; a material change is a relative change of more than 25% in the average. Return a report with metric/value/unit rows: avg_days_STATE_current, avg_days_STATE_previous, and relative_change_STATE for every considered state, replacing STATE with its code; then a row with metric 'status' and value CHANGE_DETECTED or NO_CHANGE, and one row with metric 'changed_state_STATE' per state that changed materially (value = the state code). Note anything else in the data that affects the reading.
